clue.text: Of course, I'm learner originally trained under master of composition!

definitions.text: Of course, I'm learner originally trained under master of composition!

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, so it comes after it

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, a master composer

indicators.note: the letters are drilled and put through their paces into a new order
the original letter of learner is its first, L

explanation.surface: A music student boasts that, naturally, as a trainee they studied under a great composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone who started as a learner and trained under a master ends up with a music degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor's degree in music is what a student trained in composition would be awarded.

clue.text: In a tizzy, is this fury in the extreme?

definitions.text: In a tizzy, is this fury in the extreme?

indicators.note: being in a tizzy is being in a flustered muddle, so the letters are jumbled
the extremes of fury are its outside letters, F and Y

explanation.surface: Someone flustered asks whether their rage has gone over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a tantrum is fury in the extreme, thrown by someone in a tizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a fit of petulant rage, fury taken to an extreme.

clue.text: Joint group of musicians set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised, read from the bottom

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A band of players is put together to perform at a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a club where a group plays; it is the carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry this is the projecting tongue that fits a mortise, forming a joint.

clue.text: Travelling north, one US state consumed by another, in short — here's a third!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the whole build is turned round
the pair of states goes inside the short drink

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram

indicators.note: the first state is swallowed inside the second

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York, a second US state
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A road trip northwards passes from state to state, ending in a third.
explanation.walkthrough: AL inside NY gives NALY, which goes in DRAM to make DNALYRAM; 'Travelling north' turns that round. 'In short' looks like an abbreviation signal, but 'short' is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Having named two US states, Alabama and New York, the clue points to a third state.

clue.text: Song and dance and wine fancied a lot!

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, an ado
red is wine of that colour

explanation.surface: A party with singing, dancing and wine was greatly enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' reads as entertainment, but it is the idiom for a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fancied a lot is to be loved deeply, idolised.

clue.text: Huge tailless fish, one of those seen at funfair

definitions.text: one of those seen at funfair

parts.note: a bumper crop is a huge one

indicators.note: the fish loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A giant fish missing its tail is put on show at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' takes the last letter P off CARP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgem vehicles that drivers crash into each other are a fairground ride.

clue.text: Middle Eastern paste I see in container, spicy at heart

indicators.note: the exclamation goes inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a container
ah is an exclamation of understanding, like I see

indicators.note: the heart of spicy is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A cook notices a jar of paste with a hot, spicy centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' looks like I plus a letter C, but it is the exclamation AH.
explanation.definitionFit: This sesame-seed paste is a staple of Middle Eastern cooking, used in hummus.

clue.text: Footballer's quality in game ultimately missing, what's on the end of famous boot?

definitions.text: what's on the end of famous boot?

indicators.note: the footballer's quality goes inside what is left of the game
the game loses its ultimate, or last, letter

parts.note: snap is a card game
a trait of Messi, the Argentine footballer Lionel Messi

explanation.surface: A footballer's skill shows when the game ends with a famous boot of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' suggests football, but it is Italy, shaped like a boot; SNAP loses its last letter to give SNA around the footballer's trait.
explanation.definitionFit: This strait separates Sicily from Calabria, at the toe of the boot-shaped Italian peninsula.

clue.text: Something in girl's hair, daughter after an order designed to keep nits away?

indicators.note: the daughter's letter comes after the rest

parts.words: order designed to keep nits away
parts.note: nits are lice, so an order forbidding them is a lice ban

explanation.surface: A girl wears something in her hair, perhaps to stop head lice spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: A LICE BAN is the cryptic reading of an order to keep nits away.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a horseshoe-shaped hairband, named after the Tenniel drawings of Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Not suitable to sleep in tutu, skirts removed

indicators.note: the sleep goes inside the trimmed tutu
the skirts of a word are its outer letters, here taken away

parts.note: to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer dozing in her tutu, minus its skirts, looks out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' reads as the tutu's fabric, but means the word's outer letters; 'in' puts the nap inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt is a rare synonym for inappropriate or unfitting.

clue.text: See 22
Pudding-head in antiquity, a dummy

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the relic

parts.note: a relic is an antiquity, an object from the past

indicators.note: the head of the pudding is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pudding-head, an idiot, among old relics is called a dummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pudding-head' looks like an insult; it means the first letter of 'Pudding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy or mock-up is a dummy, an imitation of the real thing.

clue.text: See 17
Shipping magnate playing blinder aboard vessel

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go on board, inside the vessel

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids

indicators.note: playing means the letters are acting out, in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shipping tycoon plays a blinder, a brilliant game, on board his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' fits the shipping surface but is a container for liquids; 'playing' scrambles the fodder to NDERBIL, which 'aboard' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornelius Vanderbilt built a fortune in steamships and railroads in 19th-century America.

clue.text: Dreamboat with cross to bear, gone less delusional

indicators.note: the jumbled letters carry, or hold, the cross inside them
the letters are confused and astray, so rearranged

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An attractive partner who bears a burden has become less deluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross to bear' reads as a burden, but the cross is X held inside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a sexually attractive person, a heart-throb.

clue.text: Tyre on, classic surrounds fine in the end

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: the classic word goes around the letter

parts.note: trad is short for traditional, classic

indicators.note: the end of fine is its last letter

explanation.surface: A classic car's tyre is put on, and it ends up fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like part of 'Tyre on' but is RE, meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre given a new tread on its old casing is a remould, still a tyre.

clue.text: True, a singular teaching on the workings of Congress?

definitions.meaning: something that is just so, an undeniable reality

definitions.text: a singular teaching on the workings of Congress?
definitions.meaning: congress here is sexual intercourse, and one such teaching is singular

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an unavoidable truth, and in the plural is the talk on sex given to children.

clue.text: Bananas can rest on top of yellow branches of tree?

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
in a down clue, the top of yellow is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bananas can sit on a yellow branch of a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' and 'yellow' paint fruit, but one is the anagram signal; the tree is a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Family lineage is drawn as a tree whose branches show descent.

clue.text: Flyer detailed every second part of final figures

indicators.note: de-tailed, with the tail, or last letter, cut off

parts.note: a trapeze is the swing on which a circus performer flies

indicators.note: taking the second and fourth letters of final

explanation.surface: An airman details every second part of the final figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as thorough but means de-tailed: TRAPEZE loses its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: These are geometric figures, four-sided shapes with irregular sides.

clue.text: Sheep penning the Guardian's business, back in time

indicators.note: the flock encloses the other pieces as in a pen

parts.note: a flock is a group of sheep
the newspaper speaking of itself says our

indicators.note: the business abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Sheep are penned while the newspaper's business looks back in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the paper this puzzle appears in, so its possessive is OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: This hour of the afternoon is a time of day, traditionally teatime.

clue.text: Happy it's inferred to hold information — not mentioned

indicators.note: the made-up word holds the letter inside

parts.note: happy can be inferred as the opposite of sad, so un-sad
I is the standard abbreviation for information

explanation.surface: Someone seems happy, it's inferred, though the news was never spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: UNSAD is not a real word; it is an invented negative inferred from 'Happy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unspoken or unstated has not been mentioned.

clue.text: Punk shaved, fancy trousers folly

indicators.note: the word pockets the other, as trousers hold legs

parts.note: lacy means fancy, decorated with lace

indicators.note: shaving trims the first and last letters off

parts.note: punk is the word shaved

explanation.surface: A punk with a shaved head in fancy trousers looks foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb here, meaning to pocket; 'shaved' trims the punk to its middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness or extreme foolishness is folly.

clue.text: Achieve something extraordinary in Spooner's fishy puzzle?

indicators.note: William Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: hake is a fish
a mystery is a puzzle

explanation.surface: An achievement so remarkable it seems a fishy puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of HAKE MYSTERY gives the two words by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something so notable it will be remembered is to achieve something momentous.

clue.text: Up in garret, needed key

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters are found inside the words garret needed

explanation.surface: Up in the attic, someone needed a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like a location, but turns the letters RETNE round.
explanation.definitionFit: The return key on a computer keyboard bears this label.

clue.text: Greek character for all to see left working alongside another?

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all
psi is another Greek letter
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A Greek character is publicly left working beside another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alongside' places PSI beside U and L; the Greek letter sits within.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Stimulating originally, if not dull

indicators.note: the original letter of stimulating is its first

parts.note: unless means if not

explanation.surface: Something should be stimulating from the start, or else it's dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull' is the definition as an adjective for a grey day.
explanation.definitionFit: A day without sunshine is gloomy and overcast.

clue.text: Topping, terrific in game shows?

indicators.note: the words show the letters inside them, on display

explanation.surface: A terrific performance during the game shows itself to be topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like an old British word for excellent, matching 'terrific'; it is the cake topping.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of sugar paste on a cake is a topping.

clue.text: Stone in rain, clean after a pummelling

indicators.note: battered letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A stone left out in the rain is washed clean after a heavy beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' fits the weather picture; it is the definition, a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish semi-precious gem is a variety of chalcedony.
